# the contributor audit: exact constant-profile obstruction



The two rectangular endpoint areas are exactly one, and the middle Minkowski rectangle has area 9/8. The actual convex hull of the two lifted endpoints has only the integer levels -1,0,1 with exactly those fibers. The specified closed oblique halfspace has endpoint areas 0 and 3/4 and middle area 9/16. Its raw mass is therefore 21/16<4/3. The zero-area supporting edge is retained as a nonempty boundary trace.

For general R>=1 the midpoint dimensions give m=(R+2+1/R)/4. Direct interval clipping gives the global tilt minimum of the endpoint sum at alpha=1/2, with value (1+1/R)/2. Thus the entire scalar family and its exact minimum at R=sqrt(5) follow from the stated elementary rational expression.

Continuous-coordinate reflection preserves this actual mixed set. Halfspace depth restricted to its middle fiber is even and quasiconcave, so zero maximizes it. The exhibited cap upper-bounds that maximum. At each extreme integer level, compactness permits any chosen ordinary through-point halfplane to be isolated by a finite integer tilt; complementary ordinary halfplanes give raw depth at most 1/2. This proves the claimed global upper bound without asserting an unverified all-normal lower bound.

The calibration in terms of actual midpoint area is algebraically correct. The positive square difference verifies that this rectangle family does not violate the weaker required edge curve. The OC target 25/36 is likewise not contradicted.

The result falsifies universal absolute J>=4/3 for arbitrary concave planar profiles, including any assertion that the same absolute credit holds at some other mixed center. It does not invalidate the six-piece replacement theorem or the all-tent theorem, and it does not settle the actual mass-dependent edge problem.

## Sections 6–7: actual middle enlargement and centroid surplus, PASS

The enlarged compatible pentagon has area 95/32. Its unchanged positive axial cap gives the stated 1/96 shortfall at the specified averaged centroid, while the bare ordinary Grünbaum lower estimate misses by 1/288. These are correctly distinguished from upper bounds on other candidate centers.

the contributor read the complete all-normal calculation for P_w. Reflection and line reversal leave exactly the three stated through-centroid cutting regimes plus the horizontal line. Their transition parameters are ordered, and direct clipping gives the stated E(t) formulas. The first two increase; the last has its unique maximum at (w-g)/(2g-w), with the displayed value. The complementary-cap minimum minus g^2 has the exact nonnegative expression (11), including the endpoint w=1+1/sqrt(6). Thus g^2 is the exact ordinary depth, not just an axial upper bound.

The inverse affine area factor 59/32 and normalized parameter 77/59 correctly describe the actual pentagon. The centroid, raw ordinary depth and positive excess over 127/96 agree with the rational formulas. Every ambient halfspace containing the lifted middle centroid contains the corresponding ordinary cap, or all of K for a pure integer normal. This establishes the required credit at that actual point for the specified example.

A minor wording correction was requested: the middle-status polygon listed in the proof is the captured E(t) polygon, not an excluded polygon. The equations and coverage are unaffected. This remains a particular shape-dependent surplus, not a universal tradeoff theorem.
